summary:
Prisons in Germany house people under statutory separation into men's and women's units. The Criminological Research Institute of Lower Saxony reads § 170(2) of the Lower Saxony correctional act as the operating rule and reports that placement matching a prisoner's gender identity has been granted only in exceptional cases; the institute runs a research project on the situation of transgender people in prison. A trans visitor who is arrested and remanded should not assume that a changed gender entry will determine where they are held.

The case of Marla-Svenja Liebich, a neo-Nazi convicted of incitement, shows how placement is decided. In August 2025 the chief prosecutor in Halle said she would serve her 18-month sentence at the women's prison in Chemnitz, with placement reviewed at intake. After extradition from Czechia in July 2026 she was transferred to a men's prison instead, although her gender entry had been changed to female under the Self-Determination Act. The authorities cited the safety of prisoners at the women's facility. Critics of the act described her gender change as an abuse of it.

Penelope Frank, a climate activist from the Last Generation group who is legally recorded as male, faced assignment to a men's prison if convicted. Reporting on her case in 2023 found that German prisons offer few safe spaces for trans inmates and that housing runs on a binary model.

Airport screening is a documented point of friction. The trans DJ and producer BASHKKA filed a complaint under the General Act on Equal Treatment over a screening at Frankfurt Airport on 23 November 2024, alleging that officers deliberately disregarded her gender identity and describing the episode as a targeted, degrading act of transphobic harassment. She provided a copy of the statement she submitted to the airport.

Access to sex-segregated leisure facilities is set by operators rather than by statute. In January 2025 a guideline from the Deutscher Sauna-Bund restricted women's saunas to people whose primary sex characteristics correspond to the facility, prompting argument about whether registered trans women would be admitted. Saunas and similar venues in Berlin have been working out their practice since the Self-Determination Act took effect on 1 January 2025, after months of public dispute over women-only spaces. The trans woman Alessia Dorigo rejected the premise that a trans identity can be claimed on a whim.

Legal gender recognition runs through the Self-Determination Act, in force since 1 November 2024 and passed by the Bundestag in April 2024 by 374 votes to 251. Adults, including transgender, intersex and nonbinary people, change their gender entry by self-declaration on three months' notice. The previous Transsexuals Act of 1980 required genital surgery and sterilisation; the Federal Constitutional Court struck those requirements down in January 2011.

Since 1 January 2019 a 'divers' option has been available on birth certificates, passports and driver's licences under the Third Gender Act. It requires a doctor's statement confirming intersex status, a condition LGBT organisations criticised, and in April 2019 the option was clarified as applying to intersex people only and not to transgender people.

The General Act on Equal Treatment, in force since 18 August 2006, prohibits discrimination on grounds of sexual orientation or gender identity in health services and in education. It is the instrument under which the airport screening complaint was brought.

Registered life partnerships have existed since 2001, carrying rights in inheritance, alimony, health insurance, immigration, hospital and prison visitation, and name change. Marriage has been open to same-sex couples since 1 October 2017, after the Bundestag vote of 30 June 2017, with full marital and adoption rights. A trans visitor whose relationship is read as same-sex under birth-sex status therefore has the same route to marriage and to the residence rights attached to it.

STOP the HATE, a prevention and empowerment campaign in northern Germany, runs a counselling finder sorted by topic, emergency guidance including an LSBTIQ* crisis line, and a hate-crime knowledge base covering underreporting, evidence preservation, witness support and reporting channels.
tangentialFactors:
In June 2025 the Federal Cabinet proposed designating Morocco, Algeria and Tunisia as safe countries of origin although LGBTI people face imprisonment in them. In August 2025 the governing coalition announced it would end humanitarian admission programmes, including the Afghanistan scheme for persecuted LGBTI people. Both measures bear on people seeking protection rather than on short-stay visitors.

In July 2025 the Federal Education Minister banned gender-inclusive language in her ministry. The Federal Anti-Discrimination Office said the instruction contradicts the constitutional guarantee of equality.

The political argument over the Self-Determination Act has been conducted largely through individual cases, and access to women-only leisure facilities is settled by private operators rather than by statute.
localsOnly:
Several states have amended their prison statutes in recent years to accommodate legally recognised gender diversity. A new § 17 of the Rhineland-Palatinate prison act took effect on 1 March 2026 without any press coverage. Writing in March 2026, a commentator argued that trans prisoners need no discriminatory special law and that ordinary anti-discrimination law should govern their placement and treatment.

The Berlin prison service publishes information for trans, inter and non-binary people in custody, setting out rules and contacts across its facilities.

A nationwide ban on conversion therapy for minors has been in force since May 2020, with penalties of up to one year in prison for practitioners and fines of €30,000 for offering, promoting or referring minors to such treatment.

Stepchild adoption became available in 2005 and successive adoption in 2013. A Federal Court of Justice ruling in October 2018 held that the non-biological mother in a married lesbian couple is not automatically recorded on the birth certificate and must adopt, unlike a non-biological father in a heterosexual couple. A bill to correct the inequality was introduced in June 2018.
outOfScopeNotes: Whether the transfer of Marla-Svenja Liebich to a men's prison was reviewed by a court, and on what statutory basis, is not established in the sources. The number of transgender prisoners placed according to gender identity, and how many states have amended their prison statutes, is not quantified. What individual saunas and similar venues in Berlin actually do, as distinct from the association guideline and the public argument around it, is not documented. The outcome of the complaint under the General Act on Equal Treatment over the Frankfurt Airport screening is not reported. Whether the proposed safe-country-of-origin designations were adopted is not stated. The current status of the bill on the parentage of non-biological mothers is not established.
